description: The New York City Department of Sanitation has sorted samples of the city's discards four times, in 2005, 2013, 2017 and 2023, to measure what the waste stream contains. The open data sets give the composition of residential, public school, public housing and street litter basket waste by material category, collection stream and season: the 2017 study used 70 main sort and 172 subsort categories, and a comparative table maps categories across all four studies. The producer is the Department of Sanitation, published on NYC Open Data. Coverage is New York City, with seasonal samples in each study year. Data download as CSV or JSON and through the Socrata API without registration, under the NYC Open Data terms of use; no licence is named. Caveats: results are sample-based estimates with statistical error, commercial waste collected by private carters is not covered, and categories changed between studies. Simulation uses: material composition for sizing recycling and organics processing capacity, and for estimating how storm debris and service interruptions change collection loads in a large city. Related records: CalRecycle waste characterisation (data-calrecycle-waste-characterization) is the statewide Californian equivalent.
